sentences.text:
Ramesh Yadav vs Jagannath Yadav on 4 September, 2025
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Jbp:42803
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Jabalpur

BEFORE  HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE HIMANSHU JOSHI  ON THE 4 th OF SEPTEMBER, 2025  MISC. APPEAL No. 4154 of 2010  RAMESH YADAV  Versus  JAGANNATH YADAV AND OTHERS  Appearance:
 Shri Prabal Singh Rajpoot - Advocate for the appellant  None for the respondents.
 ORDER

This present appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, has been filed being aggrieved with the award dated 08.03.2010 passed by the 12th Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jabalpur, in MVC No.119/2009, partly allowing the claim case and granting compensation to the tune of Rs.1,02,500/- along with interest @ 6% per annum.

entities.text: 12th Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Factual matrix of the case are that on 18.08.2008 at about 09:45 a.m., the injured/appellant while going towards Bargi Motor Stand, met Ramdayal and became pillion rider of his motorcycle.

When they reached the Tigadda, one bus bearing No.MP-15-D-5725 coming from Bargi Nagar to Mankedi respondent No. 1 rashly and negligently, dashed the motorcycle, due to which, the appellant fell down and his leg came below the wheels of said bus and was crushed.

As a result of said accident,
the appellant NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:42803 2 MA-4154-2010 sustained amputation of his left foot and several grievous injuries on other parts of his body.
The appellant preferred a claim petition claiming compensation of Rs.7,97,500/-, but the learned Tribunal awarded compensation to the tune of Rs.1,02,500/- only.

3. The learned Tribunal found that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of respondent No.1 and the offending vehicle was insured with respondent No.3/Insurance Company on the fateful day.
On account of the accident, the appellant had sustained grievous injuries and remained hospitalized for 09 days.
Exhibit-P/35 is the permanent disability certificate which was issued by Dr. Naveen Kothari (PW/2); said certificate mentions that the appellant has sustained permanent disability of 45%.

4. The learned Tribunal has awarded the compensation as under :-

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, in all, a sum of Rs.1,02,500/- was awarded by the learned Tribunal against the claim of Rs.7,97,500/-.

5. Learned counsel for the appellant has argued that the learned Tribunal erred in calculating the compensation and failed to consider the fact that the appellant was aged about only 19 years at the time of accident and has become permanently disabled.
The disability will definitely adversely NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:42803 3 MA-4154-2010 affect whole life of the appellant.

Learned Tribunal has awarded a meager sum of Rs.3,000/- for nutritious food,
Rs.3,000/- for convenience and Rs.10,000/- towards pain and sufferings.
The learned Tribunal ought to have considered the future expenditure on treatment and medicine, etc.
No proper amount has been awarded on mental agonies and hardships faced by the appellant and will have to face in future.
It is submitted that an amount of Rs.7,500/- towards loss of income and Rs.5,000/- towards general damages is very much on lower side.
The amount of Rs.54,000/- towards permanent disability is also not adequate particularly looking to the permanent disability caused to the appellant.
Furthermore, he has argued that the percentage of permanent disability has also not been properly considered by the learned Tribunal.
The learned Tribunal has committed grave error of law in holding the income of the appellant as Rs.2,500/- per month.

6. Heard.
7.
It is not in dispute that respondent No.1 was responsible for causing the accident and the offending vehicle was insured with respondent No.3 on the fateful day.
The Insurance Company has not challenged the findings of the Tribunal in respect of pay and recovery and no cross appeal either by the owner or by the Insurance Company has been filed.

The only question for determination in this appeal is as to whether the amount awarded by the learned Tribunal requires modification or not ?
8.

After going through the record, hearing the submissions advanced by learned counsel for the appellant and taking into account the nature of injuries, duration and intensity of pain,
hospitalization period and the long- Ramesh Yadav vs Jagannath Yadav on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62332040/

, I find that the learned Tribunal has wrongly assessed the permanent disability as 10%
which should be 20% and thus, considering the overall facts, in the opinion of this Court, the claimant is entitled to enhanced compensation as under:-
Amount (in Head rupees) Medical Expenses 10,000/-
Loss of Future Income (on permanent disability of 1,08,000/-
 20%)
 Future Treatment 25,0  General Damages 10,0  Loss of income during treatment 7,50  Attendant Charges 15,0  Special Diet and Transportation 30,0  Pain and Suffering 50,0  Total Compensation  9.
Therefore, the claimant is entitled to get the compensation amount of Rs.2,55,500/- in place of Rs.1,02,500/-.
The enhanced amount shall also carry same interest as has been awarded by the learned Tribunal.
The rest of the conditions imposed by the Tribunal be as it is.
10. In view of the foregoing discussion, the appeal stands partly allowed and the impugned award is modified to the extent indicated hereinabove subject to following conditions :-
" i. The respondent No.3/ Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order, failing which the execution can be initiated against it.
The condition imposed by the learned Tribunal regarding pay and recover shall remain in effect as the Insurance Company has not challenged the same.
ii. The claimant is directed to pay the requisite Court fee, if required in NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:42803 5 MA-4154-2010 the present case.
Office is also directed to verify the fact as to whether any Court fee is payable in the case; If yes, then the same may be intimated to the counsel for the appellant.

iii. On such deposit, the claimant would be permitted to withdraw the amount with accrued interest,
by filing a proper application before the learned Tribunal.
iv. The record be sent back to learned Tribunal within three weeks from this day.
v. As a sequel, interlocutory applications pending consideration, if any, shall stand closed.
